title: Short path vs. long path
idea: A signal can take the short way round the Earth or the long way. To work the long path, turn the beam 180 degrees from the short-path heading. If both paths are open, you hear an echo.

rows: True bearings and distances from one location

compare.how: The other way round, 180 degrees from the short-path heading.

traps.why: Gray line is a time of day for good propagation, not a heading. Long path is 180 degrees from short path.

traps.wrong: A map that shows accurate land masses
traps.why: An azimuthal map stretches land toward the edge. What it gets right is bearing and distance from its centre.

traps.wrong: The signal might be cancelled causing severe attenuation
traps.why: The long-path copy arrives many milliseconds late, so you hear an echo, not a cancellation.
